steps.text: Stir the oats, milk and salt together in a small pot.
Heat on medium, stirring often, until the porridge thickens and starts to bubble gently.
Mash half the banana with a fork until it looks creamy and smells sweet.
Stir the mashed banana and cinnamon into the porridge and cook one more minute.
Spoon into bowls and top with sliced banana, walnuts and a drizzle of honey.
Warm the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat until it loosens.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts and the pan hisses less.
Beat the eggs with pepper in a bowl until no streaks of white remain.
Pour the eggs into the pan and stir slowly until just set and creamy.
Crumble in the feta, fold once and serve at once with parsley on top.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion and pepper until the onion is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook until the spices smell toasty.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens and mounds on a spoon.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.
Toast the bread until it is golden and crisp and smells nutty.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt until mostly smooth.
Crush the chickpeas lightly with a fork so some stay whole.
Spread the avocado over the toast and spoon the chickpeas on top.
Finish with chilli flakes if you like some heat, then eat while the toast is warm.
Warm the black beans and cumin in a small pan over medium heat.
Mash a third of the beans with a fork until the mixture turns thick and creamy.
Heat each tortilla in a dry pan until it is soft and speckled.
Slice the avocado and dice the tomato while the beans finish warming.
Fill the tortillas with beans, avocado and tomato, then squeeze lime over each.
Sprinkle with coriander and eat while the beans are still hot.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the diced pepper until it softens and the edges start to brown.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with the turmeric and salt.
Stir often until the tofu looks dry and smells warm and earthy.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts and the pan sounds quieter.
Serve the scramble hot, topped with the sliced spring onions.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes into bite-sized chunks and put them in a bowl.
Add the chickpeas and feta to the bowl.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and oregano in a cup until cloudy.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently until everything glistens.
Let the salad sit for five minutes so the juices mingle, then serve.
Drain the tuna and chickpeas well and tip them into a large bowl.
Flake the tuna with a fork until the pieces are bite-sized.
Add the tomatoes and spring onions to the bowl.
Stir the olive oil and lemon juice together, then pour over the salad.
Toss gently until the dressing coats everything and smells bright and sharp.
Top with parsley and serve with bread or leaves.
Grate the carrot and slice the cucumber into thin sticks.
Warm each tortilla in a dry pan for twenty seconds until pliable.
Spread three tablespoons of hummus down the middle of each tortilla.
Pile on the lettuce, carrot and cucumber, with a squeeze of lemon if you like.
Fold in the sides, roll tightly and slice in half.
Bring the water and ginger to a gentle simmer in a medium pot.
Add the noodles and cook until they are tender but still slightly chewy.
Slide in the tofu and spinach and warm until the spinach wilts.
Turn off the heat and let the broth stop bubbling.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of broth in a cup until smooth.
Stir the miso back into the pot and serve topped with spring onions.
Mash the beans roughly with the paprika and diced pepper in a bowl.
Spread the bean mixture over two tortillas and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Top each with a second tortilla and press down firmly.
Cook one quesadilla in a dry pan until the underside is golden and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook until the cheese melts and you hear a gentle sizzle.
Repeat with the second one, then cut into wedges and squeeze lime over.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion and carrots until the onion is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the cumin and cook until the spices smell warm and toasty.
Add the lentils and stock and bring to a boil.
Simmer gently until the lentils collapse and the soup thickens.
Blend roughly with a stick blender, then stir in the lemon juice.
Taste, adjust the lemon, and cool before storing; the soup keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Soak the noodles in just-boiled water until tender but still springy.
Drain the noodles, rinse under cold water and shake them dry.
Simmer the prawns in a pot of water until they curl and turn pink.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce and sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the noodles, prawns, carrot, cucumber and mint with the dressing.
Taste and add more lime if it needs a sharper edge, then serve.
Rinse the rice, then simmer it in twice its volume of water, covered.
Spread the cooked rice on a tray and let it steam off until cool.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok until it shimmers and just begins to smoke.
Scramble the beaten eggs in the wok until they are just set.
Add the rice and peas and stir-fry until the grains separate and sizzle.
Splash in the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss through the spring onions.
Heat the oven to 200 C and line a tray with baking paper.
Pat the chickpeas very dry with a kitchen towel so they crisp.
Toss the chickpeas with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt on the tray.
Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until the chickpeas rattle and smell toasty.
Cool for five minutes so they crisp further, then eat within a day.
Mash the banana in a bowl until it looks like a smooth paste.
Stir in the peanut butter, honey and cinnamon until evenly mixed.
Fold in the oats until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll into twelve small balls using damp hands.
Chill the bites until they feel firm to the touch.
Blend the tahini and lemon juice in a food processor until pale and thick.
Add the garlic, chickpeas and half the water, then blend until smooth.
Add water a spoonful at a time until the hummus loosens and falls from a spoon.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle with the olive oil.
Serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping.

recipes.title: Quick lemon hummus with crunchy sticks

steps.text: Toast the oats and cinnamon in a dry pan, stirring, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Tip the oats onto a plate and let them cool until crisp.
Spoon the yoghurt into two bowls while the oats cool.
Top with the blueberries, toasted oats and mixed seeds.
Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat until it loosens and shimmers.
Cook the onion until it is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and curry powder and cook until fragrant.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Add the chickpeas and salt, then simmer until they are tender and the sauce clings.
Scatter with coriander; the curry keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion until it is soft and smells sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, turmeric and cumin and cook until fragrant.
Add the lentils and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, stirring now and then, until the lentils break down into a thick soup.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then add the lemon juice.
Taste for salt; the dal keeps for 3 days and thickens as it cools.
Heat the oven to 220 C and oil a large tray.
Mix the yoghurt, curry powder, garlic and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Turn the chicken through the marinade until every piece is coated.
Spread the chicken, peppers and onion on the tray in one layer.
Drizzle with the oil and roast until the chicken is browned at the edges.
Check the thickest piece is white throughout and the juices run clear, then rest.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat until it shimmers.
Cook the onion until soft and sweet-smelling, then add the garlic.
Stir in the sweet potato, cumin and paprika and cook until the spices smell toasty.
Add the tomatoes and half a can of water, then bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook until a fork slides easily into the sweet potato.
Stir in the beans and simmer until the chilli is thick.
Add the lime juice; the chilli keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Toss the chicken with the paprika, cumin and one tablespoon of oil.
Heat a large pan over high heat until a drop of water spits.
Sear the chicken, turning occasionally, until browned and white throughout.
Move the chicken to a plate and add the remaining oil to the pan.
Fry the peppers and onion until the edges char and the onion smells sweet.
Warm the tortillas, then fill with chicken and vegetables and squeeze lime over.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Warm the oil and garlic in a pan until the garlic smells sweet, not brown.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer until the sauce thickens and clings to a spoon.
Cook the spaghetti until it is tender with a slight bite in the centre.
Toss the drained pasta in the sauce with a splash of cooking water.
Tear in the basil and top with parmesan.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water until tender with a slight bite.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil, undisturbed, until golden and the pan stops hissing.
Stir in the garlic and cook until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the cream and simmer until it thickens slightly.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts into the sauce.
Toss in the drained pasta, parmesan and pepper, loosening with cooking water.
Heat the oven to 200 C and find a baking dish.
Toss the tomatoes, garlic, oil and salt in a baking dish.
Roast the tomatoes until they burst and smell sweet.
Nestle the cod into the tomatoes and lay a lemon slice on each fillet.
Bake until the fish flakes easily and turns opaque all the way through.
Tear basil over the dish and spoon the juices onto the fish.
Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in twice its volume of water.
Stir the soy sauce, honey and ginger together to make the glaze.
Sear the salmon skin side down in a pan until the skin sounds crisp.
Flip the salmon, pour in the glaze and simmer until it turns sticky.
Steam the broccoli over the rice pot until bright green and just tender.
Serve the salmon and broccoli over the rice with sesame seeds on top.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until it is tender.
Pat the tofu dry and fry in the oil until golden and crisp on every side.
Add the broccoli and two tablespoons of water, then cover.
Steam until the broccoli is bright green and a knife slides in.
Stir the soy sauce, ginger, sugar and sesame oil together, then pour into the pan.
Toss for one minute until the sauce clings, then serve over the rice.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and stir in the curry powder and ginger.
Cook until the spices smell toasty and bloom in the oil.
Pour in the coconut milk and soy sauce and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the tofu, pepper and green beans and simmer until the beans are tender-crisp.
Stir in the lime juice, taste, and add more soy sauce if it needs salt.
Serve over steamed rice with extra lime wedges on the side.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers and smokes lightly.
Fry the garlic and chillies until the aroma hits and they just colour.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until it is white throughout with browned edges.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until they turn bright and squeak between teeth.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar until the sauce bubbles and coats everything.
Fold in the basil until it wilts and serve with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Thai basil chicken with green beans

steps.text: Toss the chicken with the spices, garlic and oil in a bowl.
Heat a large pan over high heat until a drop of water spits.
Fry the chicken in two batches until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the pitas in a dry pan until soft and slightly puffed.
Split the pitas and spread each with yoghurt.
Fill with chicken and cucumber and eat while the chicken is hot.
Heat the oven to 220 C and line a large tray.
Toss the aubergine and chickpeas with the oil and cumin on a large tray.
Roast, turning once, until the aubergine is deeply golden and creamy inside.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water until smooth and pourable.
Add water a spoonful at a time if the sauce feels stiff.
Spoon the roast vegetables onto plates, drizzle with sauce and scatter parsley.
Heat the oven to 220 C and find a large roasting tin.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic and salt in a large roasting tin.
Add the potatoes and chicken and turn until coated.
Roast, turning once, until the potatoes are golden and the chicken browns.
Check the thickest thigh is white throughout and the juices run clear.
Rest for five minutes and spoon the tin juices over the top.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until tender.
Heat the oil in a wok until it shimmers and fry the garlic and ginger.
Add the beef and break it up, cooking until browned and the sizzling quietens.
Add the green beans and stir-fry until bright and tender-crisp.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar until the sauce bubbles and glazes the beef.
Spoon the beef and beans over the rice and serve hot.
Cook the noodles in boiling water until tender but springy, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok until it shimmers and add the garlic.
Stir-fry the prawns until they curl and turn pink and opaque.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry until it wilts and sounds less crisp.
Toss in the noodles, soy sauce and sesame oil until everything is hot.
Serve straight away while the noodles are glossy.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until a knife slides in without resistance.
Brown the beef in a wide pan until the sizzling quietens and the liquid is gone.
Add the onion and carrots and cook until the onion is soft and sweet-smelling.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, peas and a splash of water, then simmer.
Mash the potatoes with the butter until smooth and spread over the beef.
Grill or bake the pie until the top is golden; it keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat.
Cook the leeks gently until they are soft and smell sweet, without browning.
Add the potatoes and stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the milk and pepper and reheat gently.
Taste for salt; the soup keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Boil the macaroni in salted water until tender with a slight bite.
Add the broccoli for the last two minutes, then drain both.
Melt the butter in a pot, stir in the flour and cook until it smells nutty.
Pour in the milk gradually, whisking, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheddar and mustard until smooth.
Fold in the pasta and broccoli and serve while the sauce is silky.
Heat the oven to 220 C and line a large tray.
Toss the sweet potato with half the oil, paprika and salt on a tray.
Roast until the edges brown and a fork slides in easily.
Push the sweet potato aside and add the beans and salmon with the remaining oil.
Roast until the salmon flakes easily and the beans are blistered.
Serve with lemon wedges and squeeze them over everything at the table.
Simmer the rice covered in twice its volume of water until tender.
Cook the beef with the garlic, soy sauce and sugar until browned and glossy.
Wilt the spinach in a pan with the sesame oil, then squeeze out the water.
Fry the eggs in a lightly oiled pan until the whites are set and edges crisp.
Divide the rice among bowls and arrange the beef, spinach and grated carrot on top.
Crown each bowl with an egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Korean-style beef and spinach rice bowl

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the bread until golden and crisp.
Add the garlic, paprika and cumin and cook until fragrant, but do not let them burn.
Blend half the bread and spices with the water into a thick paste.
Return the paste to the pan with the chickpeas and simmer until thickened.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then add the vinegar.
Taste for salt; the stew keeps for 3 days and tastes better the next day.
Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat until deep golden and smelling sweet.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens.
Add the paprika and chilli flakes and stir for thirty seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils and water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, stirring often, until the lentils melt into a thick stew.
Season with salt; the stew keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp salt, plus a pinch for the yoghurt

steps.text: Stir the yoghurt, grated garlic and a pinch of salt together, then spread it across four shallow plates.
Bring a deep pot of water to a boil and stir in the vinegar and a generous pinch of salt.
Crack each egg into a sieve for a few seconds so the thin, watery white drains away.
Take the pot off the heat, slide the eggs in gently, cover, and leave until the whites set.
Melt the butter in a small pan until it sputters, then stir in the paprika and remove from the heat.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon, set one on each yoghurt bed and spoon the red butter over.
Season with a pinch of salt and serve straight away with warm pita for dipping.

ingredients.text: 400 g aubergine, sliced into thin rounds

steps.text: Rub the aubergine rounds with half the oil and a little salt, then grill until deep golden on both sides.
Stack the hot slices in foil, wrap tightly and leave them to steam until the skins loosen.
Peel off the skins, then blend the aubergine with tahini, garlic, lemon juice and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Toss the chickpeas with the turmeric, cumin, paprika and a splash of water, mashing about half with a fork.
Fry the chickpeas in the remaining oil over medium heat, stirring now and then, until hot and golden.
Stir in four to six spoonfuls of the dip and cook until the scramble turns dry and golden.
Spoon into bowls with the leftover dip; the chickpea scramble keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 100 g kale, stems removed and chopped

steps.text: Warm a teaspoon of oil in a saucepan, then stir in the oats and one grated garlic clove.
Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, then cook on low, stirring often, until creamy.
Off the heat, stir in the miso and soy sauce until the oats taste savoury and rounded.
Cook the kale in a teaspoon of oil until tender and bright.
Stir the remaining garlic through the kale, then tip it into a bowl and keep it warm.
Fry the mushrooms in the same pan with the last teaspoon of oil until golden and tender.
Divide the oats between two bowls and top with the kale, mushrooms and sliced avocado.
Scatter over the sesame seeds and serve; the savoury oats keep for 3 days in the fridge.
Whisk the eggs with half the salt until evenly combined, then set the bowl aside.
Warm the oil in a wide, heavy pan and cook the onion with the remaining salt until soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger, garlic and chilli and cook until the raw smell fades and it turns fragrant.
Add the diced tomato and cook until it begins to soften and collapse into the onion.
Pour in the eggs and stir slowly and constantly until they form soft, moist curds.
Sprinkle over the curry powder and coriander, mix through, and serve hot with toast or flatbread.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, for greasing the pan

steps.text: Beat the eggs until smooth, then stir in the carrot, spring onion, salt and sesame oil.
Warm a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and wipe it lightly with oil.
Pour in a thin layer of egg, swirl to coat, and cook until set below but wet on top.
Fold about an inch of egg over, then keep rolling toward you, leaving a short tail.
Slide the roll aside, oil the space, pour a thin layer under the tail, and roll again.
Repeat with the remaining egg until the roll is thick, then rest it on a board to cool a little.
Slice the roll into eight thick pieces and serve it warm.
Warm the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until it shimmers.
Add the onion, tomatoes, chilli, garlic and salt and cook until softened and fragrant.
Pour in the beaten eggs with the torn tortilla pieces and stir gently to scramble.
Fold in the cheddar, take the pan off the heat, and let it melt into the eggs.
Scatter with coriander and serve straight away, tucked into warm tortillas if you like.

ingredients.text: 700 g sweetcorn kernels, fresh or frozen

steps.text: Cut the kernels from the cobs if using fresh corn; frozen kernels can go straight into the pan.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over high heat, then stir in the garlic for ten seconds.
Add the corn and salt, and cook for about five minutes, stirring now and then, until golden in patches.
Tip the hot corn into a large bowl and stir in the mayonnaise, yoghurt, lime juice and parmesan until creamy.
Fold through the coriander and spring onions, then taste for lime and salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

ingredients.text: 100 g kale, stems removed and chopped

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220C and line a baking tray with parchment.
Simmer the quinoa in a cup of water for about 15 minutes, until all the water is absorbed.
Pat the chickpeas dry, toss with a tablespoon and a half of oil and salt, then spread out.
Roast the chickpeas for 15 to 20 minutes until crisp and golden, then cool so they crunch up further.
Whisk the lemon juice, remaining oil, mustard, sugar and a pinch of salt together in a large bowl.
Add the kale and massage it with your hands for a few minutes until it darkens and softens.
Toss in the quinoa and seeds, then stir through the cooled chickpeas just before serving.

recipes.title: Lemony quinoa kale salad with crispy chickpeas

ingredients.text: 225 g green beans, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
60 g red onion, very thinly sliced

steps.text: Boil the green beans in well salted water for 2 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Lift the beans into iced water to stop the cooking, then drain and pat them dry.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, grated garlic and salt together in a large bowl until cloudy.
Toss the chickpeas, kidney beans, parsley, celery, onion and green beans with the dressing until everything glistens.
Serve now or chill an hour first; the bean salad keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
Shake the garlic, mustard, oil, vinegar, oregano and salt in a jar until the dressing turns cloudy.
Put the halved tomatoes, mozzarella and most of the basil into a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing and toss gently so the cheese stays whole.
Move everything to a shallow bowl, scatter over the remaining basil and serve straight away.
Put the couscous and salt in a bowl, cover with boiling water and a plate, and leave to swell.
Boil the whole broccoli head for about four minutes, until bright green and tender.
Lift out the broccoli and leave it to steam dry in a colander for a minute or two.
Grate the garlic into a jar and add the almonds, olive oil, orange juice and most of the chopped mint.
Seal the jar and shake until the dressing looks glossy.
Chop the broccoli finely, fluff the couscous with a fork, then mix the two together.
Spoon over half the dressing, crumble on the feta and scatter with the remaining mint.

ingredients.text: 3 ripe avocados, peeled, pitted and diced

steps.text: Chop the onion, chilli, coriander and a big pinch of salt together on a board.
Press and smear the pile with the flat of the knife until it turns into a rough green paste.
Scrape the paste into a bowl, add the diced avocado and mash with a spoon, leaving it chunky.
Fold in the diced tomato, then taste and add more salt until the flavours sing.
Grate or finely dice the cucumbers and squeeze out the extra water with your hands.
Crush the garlic and stir it into the yoghurt with the oil, lemon juice and salt.
Fold in the cucumber, then serve now or chill for an hour so the dip thickens.
Warm the pita until soft and cut into wedges; the tzatziki keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 small shallot or onion, very thinly sliced
2 spring onions, green parts finely sliced

steps.text: Bash the cucumbers with a rolling pin until the skins split, then halve and cut into chunks.
Toss the chunks with the salt and leave them for 30 minutes so the water drains out.
Pour away the liquid, then whisk the vinegar, soy sauce and sesame oil until slightly thick.
Toss the cucumber with the dressing, thinly sliced onion, spring onion, chilli flakes and sesame seeds until glossy.

ingredients.text: 2 cm piece of ginger, roughly chopped
150 g broccoli, cut into small florets
80 g brown rice, cooked, or a 200 g cooked pouch

steps.text: Fry the tempeh in hot oil in a wok until golden and charred, then lift out.
Stir-fry the sliced onion in the same pan until softened, then add garlic, ginger and chilli until fragrant.
Add the broccoli with a splash of water, cover briefly and steam until bright green and just tender.
Stir in the soy sauce and sugar, return the tempeh and toss until everything is sticky and glossy.
Serve the stir-fry over warm cooked brown rice.

ingredients.text: 2 tins red kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Warm the oil in a lidded pan and let the cumin seeds sizzle for about 20 seconds.
Add the garlic for a minute, then stir in the tomatoes, ginger, chilli and turmeric.
Turn the heat up and cook, breaking up the tomato, for about 10 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the drained beans and water, cover, and simmer until the beans are soft and the sauce clings.
Stir through the coriander, loosen with a little water if needed; the rajma keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 300 g cauliflower, cut into bite-sized pieces
60 g green beans, trimmed and halved

steps.text: Cook the rice following the packet instructions so it is ready when the curry is.
Soften the onion, pepper and ginger in the oil over medium heat until the onion turns translucent.
Stir in the curry powder for a minute, then pour in the coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add the cauliflower, turn down the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, then add the green beans.
Simmer for 10 more minutes until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce is creamy.
Squeeze in the lime juice and serve over the rice; the curry keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 680 g portobello and shiitake mushrooms, sliced

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms into thick strips, then halve each strip so the pieces hold their shape.
Brown the portobellos in half the butter with salt, then the shiitakes in the rest, until golden but firm.
Return everything to the pan, sprinkle over the flour and toss for 30 seconds until it coats the mushrooms.
Stir in the stock, soy sauce and mustard, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer until slightly thickened.
Meanwhile cook the egg noodles in salted water following the packet, then drain.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the yoghurt and parsley until creamy.
Serve over the noodles; the stroganoff keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 1 small handful mint leaves, finely sliced

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan) and line a baking tray with foil.
Zest one lemon, then mix zest, half the juice, spices, garlic, half the spring onions and 2 tsp oil.
Spoon the mixture over the salmon in a shallow dish and leave for 10 minutes.
Mix the couscous with the leftover lemon juice, remaining oil, spring onions and 150 ml boiling water, then cover.
Roast the salmon on the foil with its marinade, drizzling with honey for the last 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, fold in the mint, and serve with the salmon and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Spiced honey salmon with lemon couscous

steps.text: Grate the ginger, squeeze its juice into a bowl, and set a teaspoon of the pulp aside.
Toss the pork in the ginger juice with half a tablespoon of soy sauce and 1 tablespoon of water.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce and water with the miso, sugar and reserved ginger in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Lay the pork in a single layer in the hot oil and leave it until golden underneath.
Flip the pork and cook until no pink remains.
Pour in the sauce and turn the pork until glossy and coated.
Pile the pork beside shredded cabbage on plates; the miso ginger pork keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 2 white fish fillets (180 g each), about 1.5 cm thick
4 spring onions, green parts, sliced on the diagonal
20 g fresh ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
1 red chilli, deseeded and cut into fine strips

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan) and lay each fillet on baking paper over foil.
Season both sides of the fish with salt and pepper, then fold the paper and foil into sealed parcels.
Bake the parcels until the fish flakes easily when pressed with a fork.
Fold the parcels open into boats and rest 3 minutes while the oil heats in a small pan.
Pile the spring onion, ginger and chilli on the fish and drizzle over the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Pour the hot oil over the topping so it sizzles loudly, then serve at once from the foil boats.

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Dijon mustard and 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard
1 to 2 tbsp water, to loosen the sauce

steps.text: Season the chicken thighs on both sides with two thirds of the salt and half of the pepper.
Sear the chicken in the oil over medium-high heat, smooth side down, until deep golden.
Turn the chicken and cook the other side until cooked through, then move to a plate.
Scrape out any loose black specks, keeping the browned film stuck to the pan.
Stir the cream, both mustards and remaining seasoning into the pan over medium heat, scraping up the browned bits.
Thin with water if needed and spoon over the chicken; the mustard chicken keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

ingredients.text: 285 g canned tuna in oil, drained
2 tbsp olive oil (or the oil from the tuna)
240 ml starchy pasta cooking water, reserved

steps.text: Boil the pasta in well salted water for a minute less than the packet says.
Scoop out a mug of the starchy cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Warm the oil in the empty pot with the garlic and chilli flakes for a minute.
Tip in the pasta with a splash of the cooking water and toss until it turns glossy.
Off the heat, fold in the tuna, parsley, lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper, keeping some chunks.
